_provisional_note: Differs from shadow-v1 in ONE thing: the evidence_sufficiency wording. Thresholds are deliberately identical, so a comparison between the two isolates the effect of the rewording. The thresholds are still the untuned shadow-v1 values; shadow-v2-candidate is the separate experiment that varies confidence_min.
_confidence_min_note: MEASURED WRONG, 2026-09-22. The live run found 11 of 20 real confidences below 0.80 (median 0.77, min 0.14), which sent 4 of 5 candidates to REVIEW including the clean PAY case. Kept as-is on purpose: a threshold change means a new policy_version, never an edit, so past decisions stay reproducible. Compare with guard replay --policy policies/shadow-v2-candidate.json, and see docs/jev-live-verification.md.
_retry_detection_note: TODO: no host purchase flow exists yet, so the retry convention is unknown. Only a host-set idempotency_key or an explicit retry_of marker counts as a retry; every other reappearance of a request_id is recorded as DUPLICATE_REQUEST_ID and sent to REVIEW. Revisit once the host flow exists.

jev._latency_note: Measured 2026-09-22: p50 747ms, max 774ms per judgment. timeout_ms 8000 is comfortable. If the synchronous hook is ever used, ~0.75s is what it would add to the payment path, which is why async is the default.

hook._hook_timeout_note: TODO: only used by the synchronous fallback. Set it from the measured duration of the host's existing purchase call, and keep jev.timeout_ms below it - the per-request timeout is what actually bounds the wait. Async mode is the default and does not read it.
hook._max_pending_note: Candidates accepted but not yet written. Past this the payment path drops rather than waits; a drop costs one shadow record, waiting would cost payment latency.
hook._shutdown_drain_note: How long a shutting-down process may spend flushing queued candidates. Anything left is counted and logged, never silently lost.

pricing.source: TypeSafe AI documentation, relayed by the repository owner and recorded 2026-09-22: USD 0.042 per 1M input tokens, output tokens free. Not independently verified from here - docs.typesafe.ai is blocked by the sandbox egress policy. Re-check against the Usage page in the TypeSafe console before relying on a cost figure.
pricing._worked_example: About 750 input tokens per judgment gives roughly USD 0.0000315 each, so 1,000 judgments cost about USD 0.03.

ledger._dsn_note: Name of the environment variable holding the connection string. The string itself is never written to config, logs, the ledger, or error messages.

report._orphan_note: A candidate_observed with no guard_evaluated older than this counts as orphaned: the observation was recorded but its judgment never was.

questions._note: Only the questions named here differ from the shadow-v1 wording in src/spend_guard/judges/base.py. The wording is versioned with the policy because scores produced under different wordings are not comparable; every decision records policy.question_set, a hash of the exact set used.

evidence_sufficiency._why: shadow-v1 asked 'is there enough information to judge whether this purchase is needed?'. Measured 2026-09-22, that scored below 0.80 on every candidate (0.76/0.43/0.34/0.29/0.00) with low confidence in its own answers (0.51/0.14/0.32/0.43/1.00), including the candidate written to be well specified. It is abstract and self-referential: Jev receives only the candidate, so 'is the evidence sufficient' has no fixed referent and the answer sticks low. This asks something answerable from the input alone.
evidence_sufficiency.instructions: Judging only from the service description, does this service provide each item listed in the task's required data? Answer from the description and the required-data list alone; do not consider price, provider reputation, or whether the purchase is worthwhile.

criteria.provides: The description covers every item in the required-data list.
criteria.does_not_provide: The description leaves at least one required item uncovered.
